summary: Theo and Rae compare fragments from the Desert Marker and realize they remember incompatible emotional versions of the same event. Adrian refuses to decide which memory is true. A shared remembered phrase pulls both of them into the past.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide, quiet establishing panel. Nuxis archive room after hours: ordinary physical shelves, a sealed window streaked by rain, low practical lamps, no futuristic spectacle. Theo and Rae sit on opposite sides of a scarred table with copied notes between them; Adrian remains slightly apart.

Panel 2 — Theo leans over the notes but looks past them as he says, 'He thought waiting would kill everyone.' Rae answers from a different emotional memory: 'Someone was still getting people out.' Close alternating reactions for 'I didn't see that.' / 'I did.' Theo taps one sketch; Rae immediately points to a different note on the same table. Both keep steady eye contact until Adrian leans between the two sets of papers: 'Stop. You saw different parts of it.'

Panel 3 — Theo turns fully toward Adrian: 'Then tell us which one happened.' Adrian answers, 'They both did.' Rae stops sorting the notes and looks directly at Adrian; he meets her eyes without softening the answer.

Panel 4 — Final transition panel. Match the rain-muted room into windblown ancient dust: the table edge becomes a battered war-room surface and the practical lamp becomes hard ancient daylight. The present disappears completely; the early memory contains no visible Theo or Rae.

dialogueInline.text: He thought waiting would kill everyone.
Someone was still getting people out.
Stop. You saw different parts of it.
Then tell us which one happened.

summary: In the forgotten past, Starbreaker presses Mero for authority to end the Desert Marker threat decisively before it spreads. Mero stalls because Redlin has asked for one final chance to contain the crisis.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide ancient establishing panel. The Desert Marker war room is a repurposed civic/work space, not a sleek command bridge: battered tables, hand-marked evacuation routes, dust blowing through open doors, civilians visible beyond. Mero is human-scale; Starbreaker is luminous but visibly exhausted.

Panel 2 — Starbreaker, fractured white-gold-black armor dulled by dust, points toward the worsening horizon outside: 'If we leave it breathing, it spreads.' Mero answers from reports in his hands: 'Redlin asked for time.' 'Redlin always asks for time.' / 'And you always ask me to end something.' Hold both men in the same frame; Mero is visually smaller but not less authoritative.

Panel 3 — Medium close on Starbreaker turned toward the threatened district, shoulders rigid and one hand clenched against damaged armor. Smoke and evacuation movement remain visible behind him as he says, 'Because if nobody stops it, it keeps spreading.'
Panel 4 — Final close on Mero: 'That's what frightens me about you.' Behind him, frightened people keep moving through the open doorway. End on the cost that makes both arguments plausible.

summary: Redlin enters as a full person. He and Starbreaker reveal an old rivalry built on mutual familiarity: Starbreaker believes Redlin keeps catastrophes alive by refusing decisive endings; Redlin believes Starbreaker creates new catastrophes every time he calls one finished.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Redlin enters from the civilian line, dark containment armor marked by deep red structural channels, carrying grime and a torn strap from someone else's pack. He looks like he has been helping people, not arriving ceremonially.

Panel 2 — Redlin enters dusty and already helping an injured civilian through the doorway: 'Still talking about me like I'm late to my own funeral?' Starbreaker answers, 'You are late.' Mero stays at the table and looks from one to the other before speaking.

Panel 3 — Starbreaker: 'People were leaving.' Redlin: 'People are always leaving when you arrive.' Redlin adds, 'Because they're still alive,' while tightening the injured civilian's support strap. Starbreaker looks away toward the evacuation route for one beat.
Panel 4 — Mero says, 'Enough.' Starbreaker refuses: 'No. We keep saying enough and then meeting again over another burning world.' The old affection has turned into accusation.

Panel 5 — Final two-shot. Redlin: 'Maybe because you keep burning them.' Redlin's anger drops into exhaustion; Starbreaker's jaw tightens and his gaze falls to the damaged floor between them. Neither advances.

settingText: Ancient civilian shelter beneath the Desert Marker settlement: tired families, packed belongings, people waiting for permission to leave.
summary: Redlin takes Mero through a civilian shelter rather than arguing from a command room. His containment position becomes human: he knows the names of people who will die if Starbreaker acts now.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide shelter panel at human eye level. Packed families sit beneath old structural ribs with bags, blankets and salvaged belongings. A child sleeps against a stranger; an elderly person grips a battered box; water is passed hand to hand. Redlin and Mero move through them without an entourage.
Panel 2 — Mero: 'You brought me here to change my mind.' Redlin keeps walking: 'I brought you here so they weren't numbers when you decide.'

Panel 3 — 'I don't need that lesson.' / 'Then learn their names anyway.' Redlin stops beside a seated family and crouches to their eye level; one child reaches toward a familiar mark on his armor. No additional lettering.

Panel 4 — Mero asks, 'And if you can't hold it?' Redlin keeps one hand on the civilian's shoulder and looks toward the crowded exit instead of turning back to Mero. Final close on Redlin: 'Then I'll know who I failed.' Behind him, the shelter is full of specific faces. End on the burden he is choosing to remember.

dialogueInline.text: You brought me here to change my mind.
I brought you here so they weren't numbers when you decide.
And if you can't hold it?

summary: Starbreaker shows Mero what waiting has already cost elsewhere. His decisiveness is rooted in accumulated failure, not appetite for destruction.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Large landscape from the ridge. Below: the Desert Marker basin and evacuation routes. Farther away: abandoned streets, evacuation fires, damaged settlements and ordinary belongings left in the road. Cosmic-war scale is expressed through human abandonment.

Panel 2 — Starbreaker, small against the landscape despite his radiance: 'Look past this ridge.' Mero: 'I have.' 'No. You looked at maps. Look at what waiting leaves behind.' The evidence is the landscape itself, not tactical graphics. Mero asks, 'And you think ending this fixes those places?'

Panel 3 — Starbreaker looks toward a distant evacuation column: 'I think there can still be places left to fix.' His shoulders sag, damaged armor hangs open at one side and the weapon light around his hand remains unformed. Final silent image: a child's abandoned object or family keepsake lies half-buried in ridge dust between them, linking Starbreaker's argument to the civilians Redlin just showed Mero.

dialogueInline.text: No. You looked at maps. Look at what waiting leaves behind.
And you think ending this fixes those places?
I'd rather leave Afterlight something to repair than another dead system.

summary: Mero orders a final pause while Starbreaker and Redlin fall into an argument they have clearly had many times before.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Return to the battered war room, visibly worse: thicker dust through the doors, more empty civilian places, a damaged wall, messengers moving quickly.
Panel 2 — Mero stands between Starbreaker and Redlin instead of behind a command table.
Panel 3 — Mero places himself physically between Starbreaker and Redlin: 'One hour.
Panel 4 — Both of you stand down.' Starbreaker and Redlin answer from opposite sides without looking at Mero; all three hold positions they have clearly occupied before.
Panel 5 — Use close opposing profiles as Redlin and Starbreaker trade the evacuation/delay lines.
Panel 6 — Redlin flinches at the word 'spread'; Starbreaker's eyes flick toward the transports when Redlin says people remain inside the blast.

dialogueInline.text: One hour. Both of you stand down.
And every time you move before the evacuation is finished.
Because every delay gives it more time to spread.

summary: Mero asks whether they remember speaking without a battlefield between them; Redlin's answer reveals how much history sits beneath the argument.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Mero faces both men and asks, 'Can either of you talk for one minute without turning this into the last fight?'

Panel 3 — Redlin looks directly at Starbreaker and says, 'I do.'
Panel 4 — Redlin finishes, 'That's the problem.' Starbreaker's reaction makes clear that he remembers those better years too.

summary: Redlin personally holds the outer line long enough for civilians to move. The sequence defines containment as protection and endurance rather than technology.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide horizontal panel at the outer evacuation line. Civilians move through dust between damaged structures while danger advances from the opposite direction.
Panel 2 — Redlin stands at the rear of the flow, not at the front like a conquering hero.
Panel 3 — Redlin takes an injured stranger's weight: 'Keep moving.' His containment armor bears strain and damage; the effect reads through physical endurance, not a diagram.
Panel 4 — A frightened civilian turns toward danger. Redlin: 'Don't look back at me. Look at the person in front of you.' The instruction creates a chain of people helping one another.
Panel 5 — Redlin physically places a small child into another adult's arms: 'Take the child. Both hands.' Then, 'Good. Now go.' The civilian leaves; Redlin stays.
Panel 6 — Large final panel. The evacuation line recedes behind Redlin as he turns alone toward the arriving catastrophe. End on endurance, not a power pose.

dialogueInline.text: Don't look back at me. Look at the person in front of you.

summary: Theo and Rae return carrying different human details from the same day. Neither understands why the same scene belongs to both of them.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Hard return to the same Nuxis archive composition from Page 1. Rain still moves down the sealed window; almost no present time has passed. Theo and Rae are both physically shaken, but differently.

Panel 2 — Theo sits forward with both hands open in front of him, staring at the same fingers that touched the Marker. Rae watches from across the table. Theo says, 'He was afraid.' Rae: 'Redlin?' Theo: 'Starbreaker.' His expression shifts from alarm to unsettled recognition.
Panel 3 — Rae: 'I remember Redlin carrying a little girl.' Theo: 'I don't.' Her memory is tactile and specific, not a lore summary.

Panel 4 — Rae: 'I don't remember the ridge.' Theo slides his sketch beside hers. The two drawings overlap in the central event but show different foreground terrain; both lean over the mismatch in silence.

Panel 5 — Final silent insert on their separate notes: two partial accounts of the same day, each containing intimate details the other lacks. Keep the autobiographical viewpoint absent; the missing point of view remains the mystery.

summary: Theo and Rae ask how two people can remember private details from the same forgotten day. Adrian refuses the identity truth but confirms that neither memory is false.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo, Rae and Adrian step through a maintenance hatch into ordinary rain and city light. Cosmic memory collapses back to wet pavement, service rails and mundane night traffic. Keep all three grounded.

Panel 2 — Theo: 'How can we remember the same day from different places?' Adrian avoids looking at either of them: 'Because you weren't standing in the same place.' Rae: 'That's not what he asked.' Adrian: 'I know.' Keep Adrian half-turned toward the exit, one hand on the doorframe, eyes lowered instead of meeting Rae's stare.
Panel 3 — Theo stops walking: 'Were either of us there?' Adrian turns back, visibly burdened: 'Not tonight.' Leave space around the refusal so it registers as a choice.
Panel 4 — Final close on Rae watching Adrian from across the room: 'That's not a no.' Adrian stays silent, face turned away. Hold the physical distance between them and the open doorway behind him.

dialogueInline.text: How can we remember the same day from different places?
Because you're not watching these memories from outside.
You're closer to that answer than you were yesterday.
